prompts.label: WHAT IS IAM POLICY EVALUATION?
prompts.placeholder: IAM authorization starts with an implicit deny. Applicable allows can permit an action, but an…

reveal.text: IAM authorization starts with an implicit deny. Applicable allows can permit an action, but an applicable explicit deny overrides allows.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Troubleshoot authorization across identity policies, resource policies, permissions boundaries, session policies, SCPs, and other controls…

reveal.text: Troubleshoot authorization across identity policies, resource policies, permissions boundaries, session policies, SCPs, and other controls that apply to the request.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An identity policy allows `s3:GetObject`, but an applicable SCP explicitly denies `s3:*` outside approved Regions.

reveal.text: An identity policy allows `s3:GetObject`, but an applicable SCP explicitly denies `s3:*` outside approved Regions. A request in a denied Region fails because explicit Deny overrides the Allow.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: "IAM policy allows it but AccessDenied remains" means another control may be limiting or explicitly…

reveal.text: "IAM policy allows it but AccessDenied remains" means another control may be limiting or explicitly denying the action.

prompts.label: HOW IT FLOWS
prompts.placeholder: Flow: Start with implicit deny → … → Return final authorization result

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Allow statement • Explicit deny • Narrower protected resource

annotations.title: Allow statement
annotations.explanation: This statement allows GetObject for the broader object path.

annotations.title: Explicit deny
annotations.explanation: An applicable explicit deny overrides an allow.

annotations.title: Narrower protected resource
annotations.explanation: Objects under this path remain denied when the deny applies.

prompts.label: IAM POLICY LAYERS
prompts.placeholder: Identity policy can grant • permissions boundary caps one principal • SCP caps accounts/OUs • explicit deny still wins.

cells.job: Can grant permissions to a user/role
cells.trap: An Allow is not enough if another boundary/guardrail blocks it

cells.job: Sets the maximum permissions an IAM principal may receive
cells.trap: Does not grant permission by itself

cells.job: Sets the maximum permissions available in affected accounts/OUs
cells.trap: Does not grant permission by itself

prompts.label: WHAT IS IAM ROLES: TRUST VS PERMISSIONS?
prompts.placeholder: An IAM role has a trust policy that controls who or what may assume the…

reveal.text: An IAM role has a trust policy that controls who or what may assume the role and permissions policies that control what the resulting role session can do.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use roles for temporary credentials and cross-service/cross-account access rather than long-lived user access keys.

reveal.text: Use roles for temporary credentials and cross-service/cross-account access rather than long-lived user access keys.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An EC2 instance profile uses a role.

reveal.text: An EC2 instance profile uses a role. The trust policy allows the EC2 service to assume the role; the role permissions policy allows `s3:GetObject` on one bucket. Trust answers 'who can assume'; permissions answer 'what can the session do.'

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Trust policy • Permissions policy

cells.what: What an assumed role session may do

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Cannot assume role -> inspect trust; assumed role cannot perform action -> inspect permissions and…

reveal.text: Cannot assume role -> inspect trust; assumed role cannot perform action -> inspect permissions and other guardrails.

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Principal • Trusted service • AssumeRole

annotations.title: Principal
annotations.explanation: The trust policy identifies who/what can assume the role.

annotations.title: Trusted service
annotations.explanation: EC2 is the trusted service in this example.

annotations.title: AssumeRole
annotations.explanation: The trust relationship permits role assumption; separate permissions policies control what the session may do.

prompts.label: WHAT IS RESOURCE-BASED POLICIES?
prompts.placeholder: A resource-based policy is attached directly to a supported AWS resource and grants or denies…

reveal.text: A resource-based policy is attached directly to a supported AWS resource and grants or denies principals access to that resource.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when the resource owner needs to control access, including many cross-account access patterns.

reveal.text: Use it when the resource owner needs to control access, including many cross-account access patterns.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Account A owns an S3 bucket and must allow a role in Account B to read one prefix.

reveal.text: Account A owns an S3 bucket and must allow a role in Account B to read one prefix. A bucket policy can name that cross-account principal and scope access to the intended resource/action.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: S3 bucket policy, KMS key policy, or another policy attached to the resource -> resource-based…

reveal.text: S3 bucket policy, KMS key policy, or another policy attached to the resource -> resource-based policy.

nodes.title: IAM conditions, MFA, and credential controls

prompts.label: WHAT IS IAM CONDITIONS, MFA, AND CREDENTIAL CONTROLS?
prompts.placeholder: IAM policy conditions restrict when a statement applies by testing request context such as source…

reveal.text: IAM policy conditions restrict when a statement applies by testing request context such as source network, encryption, tags, or MFA-related context.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use MFA and temporary roles to reduce risk from compromised passwords or long-lived access keys.

reveal.text: Use MFA and temporary roles to reduce risk from compromised passwords or long-lived access keys.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A policy allows a sensitive action only when MFA context is present, or denies S3 requests when `aws:SecureTransport` is false.

reveal.text: A policy allows a sensitive action only when MFA context is present, or denies S3 requests when `aws:SecureTransport` is false. Conditions make a statement depend on request context instead of only action/resource.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Allow only when TLS/MFA/tag/source condition is present -> IAM Condition.

reveal.text: Allow only when TLS/MFA/tag/source condition is present -> IAM Condition.

nodes.title: Access Analyzer vs Policy Simulator vs CloudTrail

prompts.label: WHAT IS ACCESS ANALYZER VS POLICY SIMULATOR VS CLOUDTRAIL?
prompts.placeholder: These tools answer different access questions: Access Analyzer finds unintended/external access paths, Policy Simulator evaluates…

reveal.text: IAM Access Analyzer can identify external access, internal access, and unused access depending on analyzer type. It also provides policy validation and policy generation. Policy Simulator evaluates whether policies would allow an action. CloudTrail records AWS API activity that actually occurred.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the tool from the question being asked: exposure, hypothetical authorization, or historical activity.

reveal.text: Choose the tool from the question being asked: exposure, hypothetical authorization, or historical activity.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A bucket might be exposed to another account: Access Analyzer helps identify the access path.

reveal.text: A bucket might be exposed to another account: Access Analyzer helps identify the access path. You want to know whether a proposed policy would allow `s3:GetObject`: Policy Simulator. You want to know who actually called `DeleteBucket`: CloudTrail.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Access Analyzer • Policy Simulator • CloudTrail

cells.what: External/internal/unused access findings and policy analysis
cells.use: Analyze access paths, unused access, or policy quality

cells.what: Would this action be allowed by these policies?
Who actually called this API and when?

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Actual historical API call -> CloudTrail; hypothetical allow/deny -> Policy Simulator.

reveal.text: Actual historical API call -> CloudTrail; hypothetical allow/deny -> Policy Simulator.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS ORGANIZATIONS AND SCPS?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Organizations groups and governs AWS accounts. A service control policy (SCP) sets the maximum…

reveal.text: AWS Organizations groups and governs AWS accounts. A service control policy (SCP) sets the maximum permissions available to affected accounts or organizational units; it does not grant permissions by itself.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use SCPs as organization-level guardrails alongside IAM permissions inside accounts.

reveal.text: Use SCPs as organization-level guardrails alongside IAM permissions inside accounts.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A developer has `AdministratorAccess` in a member account, but an SCP denies leaving approved Regions.

reveal.text: A developer has broad IAM permissions in a member account, but an SCP denies actions outside approved Regions. The developer still cannot perform denied actions. A Region-deny SCP should also account for required global services whose requests use fixed endpoints.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Administrator policy allows an action but the member account is still denied -> check SCPs…

reveal.text: Administrator policy allows an action but the member account is still denied -> check SCPs and other boundaries.

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Guardrail deny • Scope of actions • Condition

annotations.title: Guardrail deny
annotations.explanation: The SCP denies actions outside the approved Regions.

annotations.title: Global-service exceptions
annotations.explanation: Global-service exceptions must be tailored to the organization.

annotations.title: Region condition
annotations.explanation: The condition applies the deny outside these requested Regions.

prompts.label: CONTROL TOWER VS ORGANIZATIONS / SCPS
prompts.placeholder: Organizations = account hierarchy/policies • Control Tower = prescriptive landing zone + controls built on multi-account services.

cells.job: Create/manage accounts and OUs; apply organization policies such as SCPs
Set up/govern a prescriptive multi-account landing zone and apply preventive/detective/proactive controls
Set maximum available permissions for affected accounts/OUs
cells.clue: IAM allows an action but organization guardrail still denies

prompts.label: WHAT IS IAM IDENTITY CENTER?
prompts.placeholder: IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce access to AWS accounts and applications, commonly through users/groups…

reveal.text: IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce access to AWS accounts and applications, commonly through users/groups and permission sets.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it to provide consistent workforce sign-in and account-role access across multiple AWS accounts.

reveal.text: Use it to provide consistent workforce sign-in and account-role access across multiple AWS accounts.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: One corporate sign-in can provide different permission sets in different AWS accounts.

reveal.text: An employee signs in once through the corporate identity provider. IAM Identity Center permission sets then provide a developer role in Account A and a read-only role in Account B.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: One workforce portal for access to many AWS accounts -> IAM Identity Center.

reveal.text: One workforce portal for access to many AWS accounts -> IAM Identity Center.

prompts.label: FEDERATED WORKFORCE IDENTITY
prompts.placeholder: Existing corporate identity provider + temporary AWS access → federate identities instead of creating long-lived IAM users for every employee.

reveal.text: Federated identity lets users authenticate through an external identity source and receive temporary AWS access. IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce access to AWS accounts and applications. It can integrate with external identity providers. The key distinction is temporary workforce access versus long-lived IAM-user credentials.

prompts.label: WHAT IS TRUSTED ADVISOR SECURITY CHECKS?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Trusted Advisor provides checks and recommendations across areas such as security, resilience, performance, quotas…

reveal.text: AWS Trusted Advisor provides checks and recommendations across areas such as security, resilience, performance, quotas, and cost.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Treat a finding as a recommendation to validate and remediate in context rather than as…

reveal.text: Treat a finding as a recommendation to validate and remediate in context rather than as automatic proof that a change is safe.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Trusted Advisor reports a security group exposing an administrative port to the internet.

reveal.text: Trusted Advisor reports a security group exposing an administrative port to the internet. The operator validates whether that access is necessary, then narrows the source range rather than blindly accepting broad exposure.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: A Trusted Advisor security check flags broad exposure -> validate the resource and reduce unnecessary…

reveal.text: A Trusted Advisor security check flags broad exposure -> validate the resource and reduce unnecessary access.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS CONFIG?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Config records supported resource configuration history and relationships and can evaluate resources against compliance…

reveal.text: AWS Config records supported resource configuration history and relationships and can evaluate resources against compliance rules.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it to answer how a resource configuration changed, whether it is compliant, and what…

reveal.text: Use it to answer how a resource configuration changed, whether it is compliant, and what related resources are involved.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: At 09:00 an S3 bucket is compliant; at 09:15 public access settings change.

reveal.text: At 09:00 an S3 bucket is compliant; at 09:15 public access settings change. AWS Config records the configuration change and can evaluate the bucket against a compliance rule. CloudTrail can separately identify the API caller.

prompts.label: SAME INCIDENT, DIFFERENT QUESTIONS
prompts.placeholder: Bucket became public at 09:15: Config shows state/compliance; CloudTrail shows the API actor.

cells.question: Is the bucket configuration compliant now?
cells.example: 09:15 resource became NON_COMPLIANT because public access setting changed

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: AWS Config • CloudTrail

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Configuration drift/history/compliance -> AWS Config.

reveal.text: Configuration drift/history/compliance -> AWS Config.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS CONFIG CONFORMANCE PACKS?
prompts.placeholder: A conformance pack packages AWS Config rules and remediation actions into a reusable compliance framework.

reveal.text: A conformance pack packages AWS Config rules and remediation actions into a reusable compliance framework.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it to deploy a consistent set of compliance checks across supported accounts and Regions.

reveal.text: Use it to deploy a consistent set of compliance checks across supported accounts and Regions.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Example: package approved Config rules into one conformance pack and deploy it consistently.

reveal.text: A security team packages rules such as 'S3 public access blocked' and 'EBS volumes encrypted' into a conformance pack and deploys the pack consistently across supported accounts/Regions.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Repeatable bundle of Config compliance rules/remediation -> conformance pack.

reveal.text: Repeatable bundle of Config compliance rules/remediation -> conformance pack.

prompts.label: WHAT IS DATA CLASSIFICATION?
prompts.placeholder: Data classification groups data by sensitivity and business impact so controls can match the risk.

reveal.text: Data classification groups data by sensitivity and business impact so controls can match the risk.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use classification to drive encryption, access control, retention, monitoring, and incident-response requirements.

reveal.text: Use classification to drive encryption, access control, retention, monitoring, and incident-response requirements.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Customer payment records are classified as highly sensitive, application debug logs as internal, and public website images as public.

reveal.text: Customer payment records are classified as highly sensitive, application debug logs as internal, and public website images as public. The classification drives encryption, access, retention, and monitoring requirements.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Before choosing protection controls, identify how sensitive the data is and what requirements apply.

reveal.text: Before choosing protection controls, identify how sensitive the data is and what requirements apply.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS KMS ENCRYPTION AT REST?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) creates and controls cryptographic keys used by AWS services and…

reveal.text: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) creates and controls cryptographic keys used by AWS services and applications. Many AWS services use envelope encryption with KMS keys protecting data keys.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use customer-managed KMS keys when you need additional control over key policy, rotation/configuration, auditing, or…

reveal.text: Use customer-managed KMS keys when you need additional control over key policy, rotation/configuration, auditing, or cross-account permissions.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An application can read an S3 object's metadata but `GetObject` fails with a KMS AccessDenied error.

reveal.text: An application can read an S3 object's metadata but `GetObject` fails with a KMS AccessDenied error. The S3 permission may be correct while the principal still lacks permission to use the KMS key for decryption.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Encrypted resource is inaccessible despite data permissions -> also inspect KMS key authorization.

reveal.text: Encrypted resource is inaccessible despite data permissions -> also inspect KMS key authorization.

prompts.label: KMS AUTHORIZATION LAYERS
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Data resource policy / IAM • KMS key policy / IAM • KMS grant

cells.job: Access to the encrypted S3/EBS/RDS/etc. resource.
Permission to use the KMS key for decrypt/encrypt.
cells.symptom: KMS AccessDenied even when data access exists.

cells.job: Delegated permission for supported key operations.

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Principal • KMS operation • Key-policy resource

annotations.title: Principal
annotations.explanation: The key policy names the principal allowed to use the key.

annotations.title: KMS operation
annotations.explanation: The policy grants only the decrypt operation in this example.

annotations.title: Key-policy resource
annotations.explanation: In a KMS key policy, the resource refers to the KMS key to which the policy is attached.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS CERTIFICATE MANAGER?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages TLS certificates for supported AWS integrations and can…

reveal.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages TLS certificates for supported AWS integrations and can renew eligible ACM-managed certificates.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use ACM for supported load balancers, CloudFront/API integrations, and other services that need managed TLS…

reveal.text: Use ACM for supported load balancers, CloudFront/API integrations, and other services that need managed TLS certificates.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An ALB serves `https://app.example.com`.

reveal.text: An ALB serves `https://app.example.com`. ACM provides the TLS certificate attached to the HTTPS listener, so users get encrypted transport without the team manually installing a certificate on each EC2 instance.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Encryption in transit using a managed public/private certificate on a supported AWS service -> ACM.

reveal.text: Encryption in transit using a managed public/private certificate on a supported AWS service -> ACM.

prompts.label: WHAT IS SECRETS MANAGER VS PARAMETER STORE?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets and supports secret-lifecycle features such as managed rotation integrations. Systems…

reveal.text: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets and supports secret-lifecycle features such as managed rotation integrations. Systems Manager Parameter Store stores hierarchical configuration values and can also store encrypted parameters.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose based on whether the primary need is secret lifecycle/rotation or general parameter/configuration management.

reveal.text: Choose based on whether the primary need is secret lifecycle/rotation or general parameter/configuration management.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A database password must rotate automatically every 30 days, which points toward Secrets Manager.

reveal.text: A database password must rotate automatically every 30 days, which points toward Secrets Manager. A non-secret setting such as `/prod/api/base_url` fits Parameter Store more naturally.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Secrets Manager • Parameter Store

cells.use: General configuration and simpler secret storage

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Automatic credential rotation is a strong Secrets Manager clue.

reveal.text: Automatic credential rotation is a strong Secrets Manager clue.

prompts.label: WHAT IS GUARDDUTY, INSPECTOR, MACIE, SECURITY HUB?
prompts.placeholder: AWS security services focus on different evidence: GuardDuty detects suspicious/threat activity, Inspector identifies supported workload…

reveal.text: AWS security services focus on different evidence: GuardDuty detects suspicious/threat activity, Inspector identifies supported workload vulnerabilities/exposure, Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, and Security Hub aggregates/prioritizes security findings.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the service from the object being analyzed: threat telemetry, vulnerabilities, sensitive S3 data, or…

reveal.text: Choose the service from the object being analyzed: threat telemetry, vulnerabilities, sensitive S3 data, or centralized findings.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: GuardDuty = threats • Inspector = vulnerabilities • Macie = sensitive S3 data • Security Hub = aggregated findings

reveal.text: GuardDuty raises a finding for suspicious API or network behavior. Inspector finds a vulnerable package on EC2. Macie identifies sensitive data in S3. Security Hub aggregates findings so the team can prioritize response.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: GuardDuty • Inspector • Macie • Security Hub

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Sensitive PII in S3 -> Macie; suspicious API/network behavior -> GuardDuty.

reveal.text: Sensitive PII in S3 -> Macie; suspicious API/network behavior -> GuardDuty.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS SECURITY AGENT (AWS CONTINUUM)?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Security Agent, now part of AWS Continuum, proactively reviews application security through activities such…

reveal.text: AWS Security Agent, now part of AWS Continuum, proactively reviews application security through activities such as design/code security review, threat modeling, and context-aware penetration testing.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: For SOA-C03, recognize its role as an application-security finding/review service named in the current blueprint…

reveal.text: For SOA-C03, recognize its role as an application-security finding/review service named in the current blueprint; do not confuse it with AWS DevOps Agent's production-operations focus.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A development team wants automated application-security review, threat modeling, and context-aware penetration testing during development.

reveal.text: A development team wants automated application-security review, threat modeling, and context-aware penetration testing during development. That is AWS Security Agent / Continuum territory, not the production-incident focus of DevOps Agent.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: AWS Security Agent / Continuum • AWS DevOps Agent

cells.what: Application-security review, threat models, penetration testing

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Automated application security review or context-aware penetration testing -> AWS Security Agent / Continuum.

reveal.text: Automated application security review or context-aware penetration testing -> AWS Security Agent / Continuum.
